q: I've read the Oh Crap book, we'd like to use a less strict modified version. I just CANNOT with the thought of staying home all day with toddler twins in a tiny apartment.
cx: Starting with 22-month-old twins while daycare is closed for a week.

q: I again gently explained to her that we don't do diapers today but couldn't convince her to sit on the potty. She ended up peeing on my clothes while in my arms.
cx: Day one; one twin anxious, asking for 'pants on! diaper!'.

q: She clearly knows when she is about to pee, can signal and hold it for 2 minutes 😅 But what about this fear/anxiety?
Father and I are worried sick - we aren’t sure how much of it is just her independent personality or if it warrants a formal early developmental assessment
cx: Anxious mother of a 15-month-old who tunes parents out outdoors.

q: It’s hard not to compare with other children we see on the playground and wonder how much of it is just her quirkiness or are we “ignoring the signs”. Social media also doesn’t help… sigh
cx: First child, no friends with children for reference.

q: I feel like I’m drowning in toddlerhood lately and I genuinely don’t know if this is normal or if my son is just… more intense than other kids.
cx: First child, 19 months; everything is a battle.

q: He wants me specifically for sleep, wakeups, naps, comfort, everything. My husband tries, but because I’ve been the more consistent parent so I’m the default for everything. I’ve tried talking to my husband but it’s another topic that I don’t have brain cells left for.
I feel like I spend my entire day trying to “fix” problems:  \- tweaking sleep  \- analyzing naps  \- managing snacks/meals
I was able to make him sleep by himself for the last 3 weeks but today, husband tries helping and it just became worse. So now I’m assisting the nap again.
cx: Independent naps undone in a day.

q: My friends, they have a 2 yo and they asked me what was a tantrum like the other day. I was like dam life is unfair lol.
My own mom (she's the best) thought I was exaggerating but now she's been babysitting more often and she's struggling too.
cx: Mother of a two-year-old and an almost-one-year-old with very intense meltdowns.

q: We follow authoritative parenting and, tbh, we're pretty exhausted from holding so many boundaries all the time. These kids are so intense - way more than your average toddler.
I've had people tell me in the past that I must let my kids do whatever they want and that's why they behave the way they do. I absolutely do not let my kids do whatever they want
cx: Defending the label 'authoritative parenting' to commenters.

q: He woke up crying way harder than usual, and when I snapped him back in he LOST it. Full “no no no,” meltdown like I had done this to him.
He won’t play with the nanny (we’ve had the same nanny since he was born). He won’t leave me alone for even 2 mins to pee.
cx: 3.2-year-old suddenly clingy for over a month; parent works full time.

q: He won’t let me work (I work full time from office but some days from home), he won’t let me exercise, he doesn’t want to step out of the house without me.

Husband is around and an equal parent but I’m the preferred parent.  Anyone else go through this and did it ever get better or do I have to wait till my son is a teenager and wouldn’t want to be around me then?

when he's upset or angry about something, he starts trying to hit me and calls me names or says vile things like "I hope you die. I hate you. I hope you get hit by a car." A lot of times I'm not even sure what he's upset about and he won't tell me.
cx: Mother of a 6-year-old and a 4.5-year-old who has changed this year.

q: he wouldn't stop screaming until my husband finally gave in and carried him down (which i know reinforces this bad behavior but after 10 minutes straight of your child screaming 'help'  in a terrified voice, it's hard to continue ignoring that.
cx: Tried ignoring his demand to be carried downstairs.

q: he was so angry that I "left him" in bed that he proceeded to try to hit me and scream at me that he hates me, tears rolling down his face (it's mother's Day too by the way).
As you can imagine, it ends up being way easier to just carry him or feed him, even though we know we're enabling the behavior. But we feel stuck and don't know what to do.
cx: Refusing escalates and makes them late for daycare.

q: It's like my sweet, easy going boy has been replaced by this angry, rude, emotional boy out of nowhere.
When dad has him he’s chill and fun, but it’s like when I’m around He won’t listen.
It’s starting to really wear me down and as I watch both boys 70% of the time, even though I work from home, I’m getting really overstimulated and over exhausted.
We’re on day 5 of the oh crap method and put our son in trousers/pants but no underwear on day 3, the day after it seemed to “click” for him.
cx: Accidents began once trousers went on; post titled 'Serious self-doubt creeping in'.

q: What’s worrying me is that he’s never once self-initiated a potty or toilet trip while in trousers, and only did it once when he was naked on day one and two.

Should we go back to naked while he learns those signs in his body and self-initiates more? Or is the most important thing of all to make sure we have the dry pants/trousers thing down before that, as the book seems to suggest?
cx: Naked versus clothes decision the book does not settle for them.

q: Sorry I genuinely thought I read in the book that the key was not to over-prompt rather than not prompt at all?
cx: Confused by a commenter's reading of the book.

q: I’ve had charts and treasure chest and big prizes that have sat on a shelf in his view for months on end as incentive to please, for the love of god, try to poop on a toilet and he just doesn’t care.
cx: Son turned four and still will not poop on the toilet.

q: I’ve talked to his pediatrician and she says things like “He’ll get it eventually!” And “His stubbornness will serve him well someday!” And “it’s probably just gonna take a good stomach illness for him to figure it out!” And offering no other help or ideas.
I tried the “hole in the back” trick today and it turned into a screaming nightmare.

I feel like our whole family is being held hostage by poop which I know feels dramatic, but if you’ve also gone through this, I know you know what I mean. I don’t sign him up for fun things, we don’t go places, all because I don’t know if he’ll poop his pants.
The most convenient babysitter option we have available doesn’t want to have to change/wipe the butt of a 4+ year old so we never even go anywhere alone as adults.
I used to think “he’ll be fine by kindergarten!” because it was at least a long way off, but we’ve now been battling this poop issue for over a year and kindergarten doesn’t feel so far away anymore.
I’ve even fallen for those stupid Instagram ads of ladies teaching you how to get your kid to poop on a toilet (not worth it in case anyone else is getting ready to hit “buy” like me).
cx: Bought an online poop-training course from an Instagram ad.

q: I keep telling myself I’ll just stop talking about it but I haven’t been very successful because there will be days that are just so frustrating (or my husband will get frustrated which ruins any progress I feel like we’ve made).
cx: On the advice to go neutral.

q: Each time it happens, I think YES, this is it, he knows it’s not scary now! We cheer and tell him how proud we are. And then we just slide backwards again.
My first basically potty trained as soon as he saw his friends at daycare doing it so he was SO easy! I never thought it would be this frustrating for the second kid lol
We’ve gone back to allowing pull-ups for now. I feel like it’s at least a small win if he can vocalize that he needs to go vs going in his underwear.
